result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.get_node_ids()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return list of node IDs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L2945-L3007){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.get_node_ids(limit=1000) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns node IDs in the graph up to the specified limit. Node IDs are unique integers (`u64`) assigned to each node, useful for iterating over nodes or performing operations on specific nodes. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [limit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1000]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of node IDs to return. Pass `None` to return all node IDs (warning: may be slow for large graphs). Default limit of `1000` prevents performance issues when working with large graphs. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : List of node IDs in the graph, limited to `limit`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} By default, `get_node_ids()` returns up to `1000` IDs -- plenty for typical graphs: ::: {#f47bf83d .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") ) ids = graph.get_node_ids() len(ids), ids ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (3, [2, 3, 1]) ``` ::: ::: Passing `limit=` caps the result, which is useful for a quick preview on larger graphs: ::: {#f305a1df .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(100): graph.add_node(label=f"Node_{i}") graph.get_node_ids(limit=10) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [44, 88, 25, 69, 6, 50, 94, 31, 75, 12] ``` ::: ::: Passing `limit=None` returns every node ID -- safe here since the graph is small, but potentially slow on graphs with millions of nodes: ::: {#fcedb669 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph() for i in range(5): graph.add_node(label=f"Node_{i}") len(graph.get_node_ids(limit=None)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 5 ``` ::: :::
